item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports evidence-based coding rather than inferred motives. Microsoft’s [user-intent taxonomy study](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/SIGIR_2024___LLM_for_Taxonomy_v2.pdf) found annotators disagreed when extrapolating why users acted; explicit definitions and positive/negative examples improved clarity. [FAITHQA (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.349.pdf) distinguishes omitted constraints from invented or misinterpreted intent. Applied here, a proposed taxonomy is: redundant function, explicit specification conflict, unsupported ownership assumption, stale intent, and insufficient relevance evidence. Attach each label to an exact feedback span and supporting history/title/description/timestamp. Functional similarity alone does not establish unwanted redundancy; an interaction does not establish current ownership; elapsed time alone does not establish stale intent. Missing compatibility specifications warrant “unknown,” not “incompatible.” These are proposed operational rules, not an established validated recommendation taxonomy.\n\nValidation should precede prevalence claims. [Törnberg (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05129) advocates structured annotation, prompt-stability checks, and rigorous validation. Practical adaptation: independently double-code a pilot, adjudicate disagreements, freeze the codebook, then assess per-label precision/recall against a separate human reference alongside agreement and uncertainty intervals. [Conformal abstention (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01563) offers a framework for withholding unreliable assertions using calibrated error control; its guarantees require appropriate calibration assumptions and do not automatically transfer to recommendation complaints. Report annotation coverage and error among accepted labels, retaining an insufficient-evidence option. With five users per category, report audited cases and denominators as exploratory observations; population prevalence, purchase intent, and latent diversity/conformity preferences remain unestablished."}
